decision: promote as the first statistically nontrivial, end-to-end result where the small model contributes a complete multi-step informal argument and Lean certifies every numerical claim and conclusion
failure_mode: Only seven of 200 full arguments pass; five additional valid traces have a wrong conclusion, and most fluent traces contain fabricated arithmetic despite very low validation loss.

hypothesis: The trace-trained model has a substantially higher reliable regime on small operands, and additional small-only training may improve it further.

decision: promote the unmodified iteration-61 model as having a real small-number reasoning regime; reject the small-only continuation because it overfit immediately
failure_mode: Only 64 of 200 outputs get both the complete trace and final sentence right; 39 additional valid traces attach a wrong conclusion, and reliability collapses by almost an order of magnitude at larger numeric scale.

decision: use coefficient 500 as the next progressive-curriculum boundary; do not train on any opened ladder test

next_question: Is the viability boundary at six bits, or does only eight-bit preserve the small full-post-training weight changes?

hypothesis: Six-bit affine quantization is enough to preserve the learned procedure while approaching four-bit memory use.
change_summary: Quantized iteration 67 to 6-bit affine groups of 64; generated and scored the full 200-case existing trace-length suite under the same greedy contract.
decision: reject naive 6-bit quantization; the practical viability boundary is above six bits
failure_mode: Some exact-format behavior survives, but complete and core capability both degrade decisively.
next_question: Can eight-bit preserve the core result on an independently sealed test?

hypothesis: On a fresh parameter-disjoint short/long suite, eight-bit iteration 67 will retain verified-core capability with materially lower peak memory and faster inference.
change_summary: Sealed 100 fresh at-most-three-step and 100 fresh at-least-four-step cases after excluding 7,078 prior parameter triples; passed all 200 oracles; generated full and 8-bit predictions before opening the verifier; ran paired complete and core comparisons; compiled every accepted 8-bit equality and conclusion in Lean.
decision: promote eight-bit as the deployment checkpoint for the fixed-verifier core architecture, but retain full precision as the accuracy checkpoint; eight-bit is not lossless for model-complete arguments
failure_mode: Exact complete arguments lose three percentage points significantly; the 2.5-point core decrease is not significant at n=200 but cannot establish equivalence without a non-inferiority margin and larger sample.
next_question: Can low-rank recovery on the rejected four-bit backbone restore the procedure while keeping total deployment below the eight-bit footprint?

hypothesis: Eight-bit quantization preserves the frozen natural-language method representation.
change_summary: Applied the unchanged sealed 5,120-parameter readout directly to the standalone 8-bit model on the untouched 100-item five-family contrast test.
decision: retain the 8-bit deployment artifact; routing is identical to full precision
failure_mode: The router is a synthetic closed five-way test and does not offset the measured complete-argument loss.

hypothesis: A roughly 40 MB low-rank adapter can recover verified mathematical execution on the rejected 4-bit backbone while keeping deployment below the 8-bit footprint.
change_summary: Merged 1,600 previously declared medium and long development examples; froze the 4-bit backbone; trained rank-16 adapters across all transformer blocks for 300 updates using raw completion masking; retained step 150 and 300; selected step 300 by held-out loss; generated and scored all 200 existing trace-length cases.
decision: reject the 4-bit low-rank recovery; retain 8-bit as the minimum viable deployment
failure_mode: The adapter restores exact surface format to 100 percent and sharply lowers validation loss but restores only one valid arithmetic chain and no complete argument, demonstrating format recovery without mathematical recovery.

hypothesis: Verifier-guided multi-sample decoding can raise usable 8-bit core coverage without changing weights or admitting invalid arithmetic.
change_summary: On the existing 200-case trace-length development suite, generated greedy decoding followed by three temperature-0.3 samples with fixed seeds 23, 47, and 71; selected the first candidate whose complete Euclidean chain passed the fixed trace verifier.
decision: provisionally retain verified multi-sample decoding and require a fresh sealed confirmation before promotion
failure_mode: Four candidates multiply serial generation cost; this development result may overestimate the gain because the sampling policy was chosen on the same suite.

change_summary: Sealed 100 fresh cases after excluding 7,278 prior parameter triples; generated all four registered arms before opening the verifier; selected only by full trace validity; paired greedy against selected output; generated and compiled Lean certificates for every accepted selected trace.
decision: retain as promising optional inference-time search, but do not claim independent confirmation at n=100 because p=0.0625; the direction reproduced with zero regressions and all selected cores compiled in Lean
failure_mode: The fresh gain is only five cases and is concentrated in short traces; exhaustive serial decoding costs about four times greedy latency.
next_question: Can verifier-triggered early stopping and a measured cost-quality curve make the search practical without weakening validity?
